correctness.rationale: The DFS-tree classification and formulas check out. In an undirected DFS tree every graph edge joins comparable vertices; in K_{a,b} this forces an alternating spine with any surplus vertices as same-side leaves at the terminal spine vertex. For the larger-part-rooted canonical tree the exact spine loads are h_i=i(a+b+2-2i)-b-1 and g_i=i(a+b-2i)-1, while leaf-envelope load (b-a)(a-1) is strictly below h_a for a>1. Neighbor comparisons reduce the optimum to max g_i except for the balanced odd +1 parity case. Maximizing the concave quadratic gives the two stated regimes. For K_n every DFS tree is a Hamilton path and the return load is i(n-i)-1. Independent definition-level enumeration for K_{2,2}, K_{2,3}, K_{2,4}, K_{2,5}, K_{3,3}, K_{3,4}, K_{3,5} reproduced the closed formulas.

originality.rationale: The current Bourotte–Ducloz–Orponen–Seki paper introduces KLX, characterizes KLX 0/1/2, proves TW≤KLX+1, and gives fixed-parameter recognition, but its accessible abstract/full-text evidence does not state exact clique or biclique formulas. Classical spanning-tree-congestion formulas optimize over arbitrary spanning trees and therefore do not imply the DFS-restricted KLX/DTC values. Targeted searches found no equivalent dense-family formula or the biclique imbalance transition.

scientific_value.rationale: The result gives exact values for two fundamental dense families, identifies a sharp interior-to-terminal bottleneck transition at b=3a-1, and quantifies an asymptotically large penalty from restricting congestion minimization to DFS trees. These are useful structural benchmarks for a new graph parameter.

findings: The biclique formula reduces to a single concave quadratic plus one balanced-odd parity correction.
Small definition-level exhaustive checks agree with the formulas.
The source paper does not advertise exact clique/biclique values; ordinary spanning-tree congestion is a different optimization problem.
independent_checks: Reproved the DFS-tree shape restriction from the ancestor-comparability property.
Recomputed h_i, g_i, the leaf bound, the root-side comparison, and the phase boundary b=3a-2 versus 3a-1.
Enumerated small bicliques directly from the DFS/open-back-edge definition and checked clique path cuts.
limitations: The theorem does not cover general complete multipartite graphs.
It proves optimality of a canonical DFS tree but does not classify every minimizing traversal.
Because KLX is new, very recent unindexed parallel work remains a residual originality risk.
